# Pāthika Sutta (DN 24 (PTS DN iii 1))

**ID:** DN 24 (PTS DN iii 1)
**Section:** Dīghanikāya (dn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Pāthika Sutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** About Pāṭikaputta
**PTS:** DN iii 1
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/dn24

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pāthika Sutta* (DN 24, also cited as *Pātika Sutta*), titled *About Pāṭikaputta* in English translation, opens the third division (*Pāthikavagga*) of the *Dīghanikāya* [SuttaCentral]. The discourse is set at Anupiya, where the Buddha sets out early for alms and decides to visit the hermitage of the wanderer Bhaggavagotta [Emmrich 2012]. The narrative centres around Sunakkhatta, a Licchavi disciple who threatened to disrobe and abandon the Saṅgha because the Buddha would not perform miraculous feats for him or explain the primordial origin of the universe [Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995]. Rejecting ostentatious displays of asceticism and wonders, the Buddha demonstrates his spiritual pre-eminence [SuttaCentral].

Cosmological teachings form an important component of the sutta, including a recurring cosmogonic pericope on the dissolution and reintegration of the world [Jennings 1948]. In this account, beings decease from the Radiant realm (Ābhassara) and are reborn in an empty Brahmā mansion (*suñña-brahmavimāna*), dwelling mind-made (*manomaya*), feeding on joy, and luminous—a description repeated nearly verbatim from the *Brahmajāla Sutta* (DN 1) [Jennings 1948; Radich 2007; Yinshun]. In linguistic scholarship, Friedrich Weller analyzed the transliterated names and terms in the Chinese translation of DN 24, arguing from phonological features that its Indic exemplar was preserved in a Prakrit rather than Sanskrit [Levman 2014]. In the Abhidhamma tradition, the text is referenced in the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 18.1) [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels for DN 24 include discourse 15 of the Chinese *Dīrgha-āgama* (DĀ 15) and several Sanskrit fragments (SHT sutta 32, SF 46, and SF 298) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus independently aligns the sutta with the Chinese *Dīrgha-āgama* (ZH_T01_0001_011) across 76 matching segments [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, the heaviest text reuse occurs with the *Brahmajāla Sutta* (DN 1), sharing over 33,000 characters—most notably between DN 24 §2.14–2.17 and DN 1 §2.2–2.6 on cosmology—and with the *Mahāsīhanāda Sutta* (MN 12) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments also connect its narrative and cosmological segments to Sanskrit and Tibetan Vinaya and Śāstra literature, including the *Saṅghabhedavastu* and the Tibetan *Brahmajāla-sūtra* [DharmaNexus].
